videos.headline: A news-led ECB explainer: about a third of the usual Shorts views.

why.text: 35 views in 48 h against the Shorts median of 95.
Only 14% of viewers stayed engaged, though those who stayed watched 41.2%.
72% of views came from the Shorts feed, less than the usual 93%: the feed barely pushed it.

videos.next: Don't make a video because of a news event; tell a format people already watch, with a famous name.

videos.headline: Rich vs poor in rupees: close to the median, lost viewers fast.

why.text: 83 views in 48 h and 34.4% viewed, both just under the Shorts median (95, 38.6%).
By 16.7 s only 11% were left, at 'Your phone? Old in two years.'
15% came from search, more than most Shorts (2–3%).

videos.next: Keep rich-vs-poor, but in dollars and with one famous person instead of a generic raise.

videos.headline: Why billionaires never sell their stock: one of the channel's best Shorts.

why.text: 1,122 views in 48 h, 12 times the Shorts median of 95.
72.3% viewed against a median of 38.6%; 42% were still watching at the end.
Philippines 26%, India 25%, Indonesia 19%: a global story travelled.

videos.next: Tell more 'what billionaires do with money' stories in under 30 s with one clear trick.

videos.headline: The no-cost EMI trap got reach but an average watch.

why.text: 721 views in 48 h, over 7 times the median of 95.
37.4% viewed, about the median (38.6%); 35% left at 5.6 s on 'Just ₹4,000 a month. Zero interest!'
All views from India.

videos.next: Make the first claim after the hook visual and surprising, not a quoted ad line.

videos.headline: Diwali rich vs poor: slow start, then search kept it growing.

why.text: 123 views in 48 h but 330 in 7 days: it grew after launch.
54.8% viewed, above the median of 38.6%.
14% of views came from search, mostly 'rich vs poor diwali'.

videos.next: For an occasion video, publish a few days before the occasion so search can find it.

videos.headline: 'Guess what $300 a month becomes' held viewers well.

why.text: 406 views in 48 h, 4 times the median of 95.
67.8% viewed and 40% still there at the end.
The steepest fall (0.78 → 0.63) was at 'Still too low. Think much bigger.'

videos.next: Keep the guessing game, but give each wrong guess a new picture so the middle doesn't sag.

videos.headline: What the rich do with $20,000 savings: the most rewatched Short.

why.text: 1,161 views in 48 h, 12 times the median of 95.
165.3% viewed: people watched it more than once (median 38.6%).
India 39%, United States 28%, Philippines 20%.

videos.next: Short (25 s) 'what the rich know' with one dollar figure: repeat this shape with a new subject.

videos.headline: How the jeweller really earns: big reach, viewers left at the explanation.

why.text: 1,133 views in 48 h, 12 times the median of 95.
53.3% viewed; the biggest fall (0.96 → 0.65) was at 6.3 s on 'Making charges. An assumed 10% on top.'
Philippines 55%, India 33%.

videos.next: When the answer comes, show it as a thing changing on screen, not a term the viewer must decode.

videos.headline: Why billionaires can't just pay a 5% tax: the top Short of the period.

why.text: 1,175 views in 48 h, 12 times the median of 95.
44% engaged viewers, one of the highest (most Shorts 25–37%).
Viewers fell 1.09 → 0.82 at 5.3 s, on a long sentence with '$100,000,000,000'.

videos.next: Keep billionaire questions; say big numbers short ('a hundred billion') and keep the second line brief.

videos.headline: 'Which saver are you?' on a $60,000 salary did well.

why.text: 793 views in 48 h, 8 times the median of 95.
60.6% viewed, above the median of 38.6%.
India 74% of views.

videos.next: Keep the 'which one are you' format; open with the money result, not the spender's line ('Life is short!' lost 19%).

videos.headline: The Diwali car EMI: average reach, lost viewers at the price.

why.text: 133 views in 48 h, a little above the median of 95.
35% left at 5.6 s on 'Festive offer! Only ₹12,871 a month.'
All views from India.

videos.next: Local car stories reach few; prefer a global brand story (how car makers earn from loans).

videos.headline: The surgeon vs heir Short barely reached anyone.

why.text: 17 views in 48 h against the median of 95.
23.5% viewed, under the median of 38.6%.

videos.next: Two made-up people with no famous name don't pull: name a real billionaire family instead.

videos.headline: What $1 billion looks like in $100 bills: strong reach, especially in the US.

why.text: 1,106 views in 48 h, 12 times the median of 95.
United States 32%, Philippines 24%.
24% left at 6.4 s on 'Four levels to get there…'.

videos.next: Cut the 'four levels' roadmap line: go straight to the first stack.

videos.headline: Poor buys the TV, rich buys the shop: twice the median.

why.text: 211 views in 48 h, twice the median of 95.
40.3% viewed, about the median; 33% left at 'Three check-ins, and the last one stings.'

videos.next: Replace the announcement of the structure with the first payoff right away.

videos.headline: How the casino wins: big reach, the US was its top country.

why.text: 708 views in 48 h, over 7 times the median of 95.
United States 43% of views.
28% left at 5.3 s on 'Let's follow Rohan's chips through four levels.'

videos.next: How-businesses-win stories work; never announce 'four levels' after the hook.

videos.headline: Rohan's $5,000 paycheck: right at the median.

why.text: 95 views in 48 h, exactly the median.
35.4% viewed; 34% left at 5.8 s ('Five bites come out of that pay first').
All views from India.

videos.next: Personal-budget stories sit at the median: make a big-money story instead.

videos.headline: A billionaire's $1 salary: decent reach, weak hold.

why.text: 148 views in 48 h, above the median of 95.
29.4% viewed, under the median of 38.6%; 41% left at 5.2 s on 'Three levels explain it…'.

videos.next: Answer the hook's question with a picture by 5 s, without announcing levels.

videos.headline: 'Pay yourself first' with Sharma: 2.5 times the median.

why.text: 238 views in 48 h against the median of 95.
43.8% viewed, above the median of 38.6%.
99% of views from the Shorts feed.

videos.next: Show the two pots side by side earlier; 24% left at 6 s during Rohan's way.

videos.headline: Which money level are you on: near the median, falling at each level.

why.text: 125 views in 48 h, a little above the median of 95.
33.3% viewed, under the median; at 10.8 s viewers fell 0.55 → 0.36 at 'Level two'.

videos.next: Use levels only for real money ladders with famous names (the formats rule), not a budgeting checklist.

videos.headline: Every burger pays McDonald's rent: good hold for a 69 s Short.

why.text: 469 views in 3 days (no 48 h figure yet).
48.7% viewed at 69 s, above the median of 38.6%; 52% engaged.
Viewers fell 1.10 → 0.90 at 5.9 s on 'Picture one restaurant…'.

videos.next: Drop 'Picture…' warm-ups (now a rule) and start the first clue straight away.

videos.headline: Too few long videos to judge: 6 views in 48 h.

why.text: 6 views in 48 h and 13.3% viewed; the long-video median is 1 view and 0.6% (3 videos).
Traffic came from the channel page (36%) and other pages, not search or suggestions.

videos.next: Long videos need a search title people type: name the question exactly as asked.

videos.headline: 3 views in a week: the long video was not found.

why.text: 1 view in 48 h and 0% viewed (median of 3 long videos: 1 view).
Half the views came from search.

videos.next: Title long videos as the exact search ('how billionaires avoid tax') and link them from a Short.

videos.headline: How airlines make money: 2 views.

why.text: 1 view in 48 h, 2 in total; 0.6% viewed.
Its only search was 'how airlines make money': the title works for search but it has no reach yet.

videos.next: Point a Short at each long video (related video link) so it gets its first viewers.

videos.headline: The 10,000-years billion is now above the typical Short on both views and how much of it people watch.

why.text: 54.8% viewed against a median of 39.2% for our 35 measured Shorts, even at 60 s long.
188 views on the public counter after about 3 days, against a median of 109 views in 48 hours (34 measured Shorts); no 48-hour figure from Analytics yet.
Hook hold 1.148: more viewers were there at 3 s than at the start (rewatches of the opening).

videos.next: Keep the 'how long would it take' idea but tell it in 28-35 s: length band 28-35 has a median of 721 views in 48 hours (7 Shorts).

videos.headline: Google paying Apple is a famous big-money story, but at 63 s it got a third of a typical Short's views.

why.text: 33 views on the public counter after about 2.4 days, against a median of 109 views in 48 hours for our 34 measured Shorts.
It runs 63 s. The variant system's numbers: Shorts of 20-27 s have a median of 770 views in 48 hours (4 videos), 28-35 s 721 (7).
No % viewed, traffic or drop points yet: YouTube Analytics hasn't reported this video.

videos.next: Retell the Google-Apple deal as a 28-35 s Short with the $20B figure in the first line; the topic itself fits the big-money option (median 907 views, 10 videos).

videos.headline: Buffett and Coca-Cola is a famous name, but at 61 s it stayed under the typical Short's views.

why.text: 62 views on the public counter after about 2.1 days, against a median of 109 views in 48 hours for our 34 measured Shorts.
It runs 61 s and opens with a myth hook; the myth hook has no measured videos yet in the variant system, the question hook has a median of 423 (5 videos).
No % viewed, traffic or drop points yet: YouTube Analytics hasn't reported this video.

videos.next: Make the next famous-investor story 20-35 s with a question hook, as the current defaults say.

videos.headline: The $10 gym Short is the channel's best start in weeks: 908 views in its first 48 hours, 27 s long.

why.text: 908 views at 48 hours on the hourly counter, about 12.5× the median of 72.5 for our 42 measured Shorts.
At 27 s it is the shortest recent Short, inside the 20-35 s band the October hits came from.
6 likes and 0 subscribers so far; YouTube Analytics has not reported it yet, so no % viewed, traffic or drop points.

videos.next: Tell another famous business's 'we profit when you don't use it' model in 25-30 s with the same myth hook.

videos.headline: Viewers who saw the $1M-a-day fortune watched almost all of it, but few were shown it.

why.text: 76.2% viewed against a median of 40.2%, the best of the recent Shorts.
Non-subscribers watched 90.3% on average.
Only 32 views at 48 hours against a median of 72.5; 72% of views came from the Shorts feed.

videos.next: Keep the 35 s spend-a-fortune maths but put a famous name (Musk, Bezos) in the title to win the first swipe.

videos.headline: The $5,000 bonus Short held viewers but stayed small, like other personal-money titles.

why.text: 27 views at 48 hours, against a median of 72.5.
52.5% viewed against a median of 40.2%.
All 11 views Analytics has so far came from the Shorts feed, none from search.

videos.next: Frame the same idea through a famous rich person instead of 'your bonus'.

videos.headline: The Line in Saudi Arabia held viewers well and found people searching for it.

why.text: 63.3% viewed against a median of 40.2%; 49 views at 48 hours against 72.5.
23.1% of views came from YouTube search, mostly 'the line saudi arabia' (5 of 8 searches).
The steepest drop, 21.7% of viewers, came at 4.9 s on 'Saudi Arabia planned The Line, one straight city 170 kilometres long.'

videos.next: Name the megaproject people search for in the title and cut the plain set-up line at 5 s.

videos.headline: The Elon Musk Short barely reached anyone in its first two days.

why.text: 15 views at 48 hours, against a median of 72.5.
47.1% viewed against a median of 40.2%, so the few who saw it stayed.
It runs 44 s, above the 20-35 s band.
